explain.say: What if you could use electricity to split a compound apart? That is electrolysis. Look at the board. First, the ions must be free to move, so you melt the compound or dissolve it in water. Here it is copper chloride solution.

explain.say: See the battery? You dip two rods, called electrodes, into the solution and switch on. One is positive, called the anode. One is negative, called the cathode. What do you think the charged ions will do?

explain.say: The negative one! Look at the cathode. Each copper ion gains two electrons and becomes copper metal, a pink coating. At the anode, chloride ions lose electrons and bubble off as chlorine gas, which smells like a pool. Can you see why labs use a fume cupboard?

explain.say: Great work! Here you can see the pattern: metals form at the cathode, non-metals at the anode. Wow: electrolysis makes aluminium, silver-plates cutlery, and purifies the copper in the wires of your phone.

faq.q: Why must the compound be melted or dissolved?
faq.a: In a solid, the ions are locked in place. Melting or dissolving frees them to move to the electrodes, which is what lets the current flow.

faq.q: Which ions go to which electrode?
faq.a: Positive ions, like metal ions, move to the negative cathode. Negative ions, like chloride, move to the positive anode.
asks: Where do positive ions go in electrolysis?

faq.a: An electrolyte is a molten or dissolved ionic compound that conducts electricity and is split up by it, like copper chloride solution.
At the cathode, positive ions gain electrons. Copper ions become copper metal, which coats the electrode.
asks: What forms at the negative electrode?

faq.a: Electroplating uses electrolysis to coat an object with a thin layer of metal, like silver on cutlery or chromium on taps. The object is made the cathode.

facts: In electrolysis, positive ions move to the cathode (negative electrode) and negative ions move to the anode (positive electrode).
Electrolysis of copper chloride solution produces copper at the cathode and chlorine gas at the anode.

quiz.show: In the electrolysis of molten lead bromide, what forms at the cathode?
quiz.why: Positive lead ions go to the negative cathode and become lead metal.

wrong.1: Bromide ions are negative, so bromine forms at the anode.

quiz.say: Why does solid sodium chloride not conduct electricity?
quiz.show: Why does solid sodium chloride not conduct electricity?
quiz.why: In a solid the ions are fixed in the lattice, so no current flows.

wrong.0: Sodium chloride is made of ions, but in a solid they are fixed.
wrong.1: Sodium chloride is an ionic compound, not a metal.
